_meta.title: GridWise — Adversarial Fine-Tuning Case Pack (team-authored)
_meta.description: Ten hand-built cases targeting interpretation weak spots: trailing-midnight windows, energy-worded distractors, state-not-directive notes, 24-hour times, zero/100% factors, fraction-word reserves, and combined directives. Same schemas as the Problem Statement. Each case carries the expected machine-checkable interpretation; schedules are validated by replay (no reference costs — any valid optimal plan is accepted).

cases.label: Trailing-midnight charging ban
cases.rationale: Windows ending at midnight ('11 PM until midnight') must resolve to [23]. Tokenizers that map midnight->0 produce an end<=start window and wrongly fall back to no_op.

operator_notes: Do not charge the battery from 11 PM until midnight for overnight safety checks.

cases.label: Energy-worded distractor plus evening grid cap
cases.rationale: A note mentioning solar at noon with no operational instruction must be no_op despite energy nouns. The real cap uses 'at most' phrasing with a 'through' window.

operator_notes: The solar eclipse viewing party is at noon on the main field.
Grid intake must stay at most 150 kWh per hour from 6 PM through 9 PM.

cases.label: Half-cut solar in 24-hour times
cases.rationale: 'Cut in half' carries no % sign; the window uses 24-hour clock with no meridiem. Factor must be 0.5 for hours [13,14].

operator_notes: Rooftop output will be cut in half between 13:00 and 15:00 due to inverter testing.

cases.label: Zero-solar outage plus fraction-word reserve plus distractor
cases.rationale: 'Fully offline' means factor 0 (not a guess); 'a quarter of capacity' must scale by the 240 kWh capacity into 60 kWh; the library note is no_op.

operator_notes: No solar at all from 10 AM until noon; the array will be fully offline.
Keep the battery above a quarter of capacity from 6 PM until 10 PM for night operations.
The library fine payment counter moves to room 12.

cases.label: Must-not-supply discharge ban
cases.rationale: Discharge bans paraphrased without the word 'discharge' ('must not supply load') must still map to no_discharge_window.

operator_notes: The battery must not supply load from 5 PM until 7 PM during relay work.

cases.label: State-not-directive note is no_op
cases.rationale: 'Will be fully charged by 6 PM' states an outcome with no window, no value, and no prohibition. Inventing a reserve or window here would violate the no-invention guardrail.

operator_notes: The battery will be fully charged by 6 PM today.

cases.label: 100% reduction plus 24-hour grid cap
cases.rationale: '100% reduction' leaves factor 0 (usable fraction remaining, not the loss). Cap window uses bare 24-hour times.

operator_notes: Expect a 100% reduction in PV output from 11 AM to 2 PM.
Feeder intake capped at 170 kWh each hour between 18:00 and 21:00.

cases.label: Through-window reserve with maintain wording
cases.rationale: 'Through 10 PM' is end-exclusive at 22:00, giving [18,19,20,21]. 'Maintain' must count as a reserve verb.

operator_notes: Maintain at least 90 kWh in storage from 6 PM through 10 PM for the data center.

cases.label: Till-connector dawn outage plus one-tenth solar
cases.rationale: 'Till' must work as a range connector; 'one-tenth of forecast' is factor 0.1 for [12,13].

operator_notes: Charger outage from 2 AM till 5 AM.
Usable rooftop solar will be just one-tenth of forecast from noon to 2 PM.

cases.label: Double no-invention trap
cases.rationale: A solar noun plus a time with no stated impact ('crew arrives') and a food note with a time ('lunch at noon') must both be no_op. Guessing a 0.5 factor here is the failure mode.

operator_notes: Panel washing crew arrives at 9 AM.
The cafeteria will serve lunch at noon.

cases.label: Leading-midnight charging ban
cases.rationale: Windows starting at midnight ('from midnight until 5 AM') must resolve to [0,1,2,3,4]. Mirrors the trailing-midnight bug in the other direction.

operator_notes: No charging from midnight until 5 AM while the meter is recalibrated.

cases.label: 12 AM cheap-hour charging ban
cases.rationale: '12 AM' is hour 0, so the ban covers [0,1,2] — the cheapest hours, forcing the optimizer to charge elsewhere. Tests 12 AM normalization plus economically binding constraints.

operator_notes: Charging is suspended between 12 AM and 3 AM for contactor replacement.

cases.label: 12 PM curtailed-to-30% PV note
cases.rationale: '12 PM' is hour 12 (not midnight); 'PV' abbreviation must count as solar; 'curtailed to 30%' is a drop-to reading giving factor 0.3.

operator_notes: PV output will be curtailed to 30% from 12 PM to 2 PM for grid compliance.

cases.label: Bare percent-of-battery reserve
cases.rationale: 'Keep at least 50% in the battery' states no kWh and no word 'capacity' — the percentage must still scale by the 200 kWh capacity into 100 kWh.

operator_notes: Keep at least 50% in the battery from 6 PM to 9 PM.

cases.label: Two solar notes, same request
cases.rationale: Two solar_reduction directives in one request must both be extracted and both applied (optimizer keeps the tighter factor per hour).

operator_notes: Morning cloud will cut solar in half from 10 AM to noon.
Afternoon haze will bring rooftop output down to a quarter from 1 PM to 3 PM.

cases.label: Three-quarters solar output
cases.rationale: 'Three-quarters of forecast' is factor 0.75 — a fraction word the parser did not previously know. Guessing or no_op here are both failures.

operator_notes: Dust will hold rooftop output to about three-quarters of forecast from 9 AM to 11 AM.

cases.label: Not-fall-below reserve wording
cases.rationale: 'Must not fall below 100 kWh' is a reserve requirement phrased as a prohibition, from 7 PM to 10 PM.

operator_notes: Battery must not fall below 100 kWh from 7 PM to 10 PM.

cases.label: Ceiling cap plus numeric distractor
cases.rationale: 'Ceiling' must read as a grid cap; 'Book room 404 at 5 PM' carries numbers and a time but zero energy content and must be no_op.

operator_notes: Evening grid ceiling is 160 kWh from 6 PM to 9 PM.
Book room 404 at 5 PM.

cases.label: Forbidden-to-charge with leading-zero 24h times
cases.rationale: 'Forbidden' is a prohibition the parser did not previously recognize; '02:00' tests zero-padded 24-hour times.

operator_notes: It is forbidden to charge the battery between 02:00 and 05:00.

cases.label: Zero solar output during outage
cases.rationale: 'Zero solar output' with an outage cue means factor 0 for [13,14] — distinct from a panel-mention with no impact claim.

operator_notes: Expect zero solar output from 1 PM to 3 PM during the outage.
